transcript: Despite living in New York since 2019, I somehow have never seen Cat Cohen perform live. If you don't know who Cat Cohen is, she's a staple of the New York cabaret scene, often performing at places like Joe's Pub Club C-ming. She has a Netflix special and now her latest show, Broad Strokes, is playing off Broadway at the Lucille Lortel Theatre. This show is about her experiences having a stroke at the age of 30. Although there is many a Tangent to pat out the 65 minute run time, which does fly by due to the brisk nature of Cohen's delivery and some very sleek direction from Alex Timbers. The set is actually pretty lavish for a one person show. The set is by Derek McLane and has a very purple Gothic aesthetic, very reminiscent of his work on Death Becomes Her, but it never pulls focus from Cohen herself. If I had to describe her comedy in a word, it would be millennial, as this show is filled to the brim with millennial slang along with some comedic musical numbers in the vein of Rachel Bloom. The songs are very fun, but they do sometimes feel a little bit shoe horned in. Despite that, I still found myself very delighted every time she would start a new song, and overall I had a really great time at broad strokes. It's not exactly reinventing the wheel in terms of comedy, nor does it get quite as introspective as the concept Might imply, but if you enjoy that millennial online style humor and are just looking for a fun night out, this certainly fits the Bill and will be getting a Broadway Ben recommendation.
